subject: Activity ledger access window and on-call evidence flow
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@greenline.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@greenline.health
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activity ledger access window and on-call evidence flow

Hi Soojin,

We're preparing for a SIG/CAIQ review next month and our audit team has a couple of precise asks around admin activity and on-call evidence. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?

1) Exact event classes that are captured in the "activity ledger" (we need to map to SIG Control 10.x): role changes, API key lifecycle, tenant-level config changes, operator session records, KV/cache invalidations, job/scale events, model pin/rollout, and request-level metadata (request id, model, token count). Are there additional categories we should list?

2) Default retention windows and options to extend (we need an answer both for hosted API customers and for Dedicated customers).

3) Export formats you support (manifest, JSONL, Parquet, checksums, signed attestations) and delivery options (S3 presigned, SFTP, direct download link).

4) Redaction/PII handling — how do you handle user identifiers inside prompt text or metadata, and can we request redaction for a scoped export?

5) For on-call evidence: if an incident ticket references a time window and operator session id, what is the typical turnaround and chain-of-custody you provide?

We'd like a short runbook we can attach to the SIG packet. If you have an example export manifest and a matrix that maps event categories to retention/fields, please attach.

Thanks — appreciate a concise run-of-show we can include in the packet.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Security Manager, Greenline Health
compliance@greenline.health

Subject: Re: Activity ledger access window and on-call evidence flow

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise runbook and answers you can drop into the SIG/CAIQ packet. I attached a compact "access-window-matrix.xlsx" and an abbreviated export playbook for the two most common paths.

Summary (short):
- What we log: tenant and operator administrative events (role/grant/revoke), API key lifecycle (create/rotate/revoke), model pinning/rollouts, config changes (routing, quotas, SSO changes), autoscale and pool events, operator session start/stop with session id, operator command traces (when operator-assisted actions occur), KV/prefix cache invalidation, and per-request metadata (request id, model, token counts, truncated prompt hash).
- Default retention: Hosted API default = 90 days; Dedicated = configurable with standard tiers (90d, 180d, 365d) under reserved contracts; Private (VPC/on-prem) = customer-managed. Longer retention options can be added for hosted via an add-on (up to 3 years) with pricing and either encrypted archival or hot retention for e-discovery windows.
- Export formats & delivery: JSONL (line-delimited events), Parquet (columnar for analytics), gzipped JSONL for large windows; manifest.json with HMAC-SHA256 signatures and a signed manifest (PDF attestation) on request. Delivery options: S3 presigned object(s) + manifest, SFTP push, or time-limited HTTPS bundle. We also offer a streaming export feed for near-real-time audit ingest (partnered SIEM ingestion).
- PII & redaction: Our standard export includes prompt hashes (SHA256) not raw prompt text for customer data flagged as PII. Metadata fields that are high-risk (user_email, ip_address) are available in exports only if the customer has agreed to that retention in their contract; otherwise we provide hashed/partial redaction. For ad-hoc redaction requests we can run scoped scrubbing on export bundles (redaction exception: must be agreed in bunlding order and may require a separate attestation).
- On-call evidence flow: For an incident we can produce an "incident snapshot" (timebox + operator session ids + associated request ids + manifest + chain-of-custody) within 48–72 business hours for Hosted ad-hoc requests. The snapshot includes: event bundle (JSONL/Parquet), manifest with checksums, preservation notes (timezone normalization applied), and a signed attestation PDF. For Dedicated, SLAs can be contracted to 24h with reserved-day-of-week pushes.

Operational notes (details you can paste):
- Time normalization: all events are recorded in UTC and we include the original zone offset where available. We canonicalize timestamps to ISO-8601 (UTC) in exports and provide a timezone map in the manifest.
- Sampling & volume: for very large tenants we provide sampling guidance and can provide a representative sample plus a full on-demand retrieval.
- Chain of custody: every export includes: manifest.json (file list + checksums + HMAC), export signing certificate alias, requester identity (Redwood operator id), and delivery channel proof (S3 signed URL or SFTP log).

Next steps / ask from you:
1) Which retention tier Greenline wants for the SIG packet (90/180/365 or custom)?
2) Do you need raw prompt text included for the review (we generally advise hashes unless contractually permitted)?
3) Would you like us to produce a one-off incident snapshot for a short sample window to include as sample evidence?

I'll loop in Karthik for the export runbook and Ben for the attestation/manifest process.

Regards,

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Activity ledger access window and on-call evidence flow

Hi Alex — quick follow-up with concrete export options and a sample command you'd provide to your SOC team.

Two delivery options we recommend:
1) Ad-hoc incident snapshot (fast path): provide time window (ISO UTC), list of operator session ids (optional), and ticket id. We produce a gzipped JSONL bundle + manifest and provide an S3 presigned URL valid for 7 days. Turnaround: 24–72 business hours (Hosted default 48–72).

Sample request (email to redwood-evidence@redwood.ai):
- Tenant: greenline-prod
- Window: 2027-04-15T03:00:00Z to 2027-04-15T07:00:00Z
- Fields: include_operator_session_ids=true, include_raw_prompts=false, include_ip_addresses=false
- Delivery: s3:greenline-evidence-bucket/path/
- Ticket: GL-5729 (for chain-of-custody)

2) Scheduled snapshot (defensive path): weekly snapshot pushed to your S3 with retention tags and HMAC manifests. Useful for audit packets — we can include a golden sample for SIG packet and a signed attestation on each weekly push.

Notes on redaction exceptions: we can do per-export redaction but it requires an internal runbook step (manual review) and a signed request from your security contact. That process is documented in the attached export-playbook.md (see section 3).

Operational command example (for our on-call engineers):
redwood export create --tenant greenline-prod --from 2027-04-15T03:00:00Z --to 2027-04-15T07:00:00Z --fields request_id,model,operator_session,action --format jsonl.gz --manifest --hmac-sign 

Proof and attestation: when you request an incident snapshot we attach manifest.json and a signed-handshake.pdf (attestation) that lists who performed the extraction and the HMAC fingerprint.

Ben, if you can confirm the HMAC fingerprinting algorithm and retention tagging we recommended 90d default + opt-in archival to 3y for Greenline.

Thanks — happy to set up a short 20m call if you want to walk the export flow live.

—Karthik
